issue_1_arm_a_validation_discrepancy.explanation: Evaluated on two distinct validation audio distributions: baseline generator (val_manifest_6class.csv, 100% at best ep, 96.76% at ep 25) vs onset-aware generator (val_manifest_onset_aware.csv, 82.87%).

issue_2_arm_b_zero_recall_on_older_holdo.explanation: Controlled 2x2 diagnostic proves Arm B's 0.0% TRAI recall on baseline clips is robust to temporal alignment (0.0% when centered at 246ms, 0.0% when left-aligned at 0ms). Arm B requires the 25ms closure and burst acoustics to separate TRAI from PHAI. However, alignment was confounded across generators for other classes (e.g. XUONG jumped from 16.7% to 100% when left-aligned, and Arm A dropped from 34% to 0% when onset audio was centered).

DISC-01.title: Arm A Validation Accuracy Discrepancy
DISC-01.reported_issue: Arm A validation accuracy was reported as 96.76% (best ep 100.00%) in Table 3.1 and 82.87% in Table 4.1.
DISC-01.root_cause: The two tables evaluated Arm A on two distinct validation audio distributions: Table 3.1 evaluated on 'val_manifest_6class.csv' (V3 baseline generator without stop closure), whereas Table 4.1 evaluated on 'val_manifest_onset_aware.csv' (V4 onset-aware generator with 25ms stop closure).

DISC-02.title: Arm B Zero TRAI Recall on Older Holdouts & Alignment Confound
DISC-02.reported_issue: Arm B exhibited 0.0% TRAI recall on Historical 144, Historical 216, V2 Fresh Holdout, and V3 Fresh Holdout. Was this caused by the 25ms closure gap, or confounded by temporal alignment (center-padded vs left-aligned)?
DISC-02.root_cause: Controlled 2x2 diagnostic resolves the confound: (1) On baseline clips, Arm B achieves 0.0% TRAI recall under BOTH center-aligned (246ms onset) and left-aligned (0ms onset) conditions (36/36 predicted as PHAI in both). However, the 25ms stop closure alone cannot be concluded as the sole proven cause, because baseline and onset-aware generators co-vary across multiple acoustic dimensions simultaneously (burst frequency, formant transitions, pitch contours, and spectral envelope). (2) Temporal alignment strongly affects other classes and models: XUONG on Arm B jumped from 16.7% to 100.0% when left-aligned, and Arm A dropped from 34.0% to 0.0% when onset-aware TRAI was centered. Therefore, alignment was a co-occurring confound and causal attribution remains unresolved.

DISC-03.title: Lineage Verification in Historical Schema
DISC-03.reported_issue: Automatic lineage tracking cannot be validated on historical benchmark manifests.
DISC-03.root_cause: The historical 16-column benchmark schema does not contain 'parent_recording_id' or 'session_id' columns. These columns are only specified in the proposed human-campaign 24-column schema.

DISC-04.title: Pitch Augmentation Terminology Discrepancy
DISC-04.reported_issue: Arm C description implied isolated pitch augmentation.
DISC-04.root_cause: Implementation uses linear rate resampling (librosa/scipy resample), which scales duration, pitch, and formants jointly rather than performing phase-vocoder pitch transposition.

DISC-05.title: Arithmetic Contradictions in Markdown Report Recall vs Accuracy / Misses
DISC-05.reported_issue: In the preliminary V4 report, Arm B Hist 144 reported recalls 0%, 100%, 100%, 100% implied 108/144 = 75.0% accuracy vs reported 54.17%; Arm C Hist 144 reported recalls 52.8%, 75%, 100%, 100% implied 118/144 = 81.94% accuracy vs reported 58.33%; Arm A Val Onset-Aware reported recalls 22.2%, 100%, 100%, 100% implied 28 target misses vs reported 37 misses.
DISC-05.root_cause: In the preliminary Markdown report, XUONG recall was mistakenly copy-pasted as 100.0% instead of its actual value from the confusion matrix. The true values are: Arm B Hist. 144 XUONG recall is 16.7% (6/36, 30 predicted as LEN), yielding 0 + 36 + 36 + 6 = 78/144 = 54.17%; Arm C Hist. 144 XUONG recall is 5.6% (2/36, 34 predicted as LEN), yielding 19 + 27 + 36 + 2 = 84/144 = 58.33%; Arm A Val Onset-Aware XUONG recall is 75.0% (27/36, 9 predicted as LEN), yielding 8 + 36 + 36 + 27 = 107 correct target, exactly 144 - 107 = 37 misses, and (107 + 72)/216 = 179/216 = 82.87% accuracy.

DISC-06.title: Waveform Closure RMS vs Silence Threshold Contradiction
DISC-06.reported_issue: Table 4 of the audit report claimed a 25ms strictly silent closure (< 0.005) but reported an RMS of 0.05551, which is mathematically impossible for an interval where all samples are < 0.005.
DISC-06.root_cause: The audit script used `active = np.where(abs_a > 0.01)[0]` to detect speech start. Because the true closure gap (samples 0 to 400) has a maximum absolute amplitude of 0.001740, this threshold check skipped the closure gap and evaluated samples 400 to 800 (the post-closure burst and vowel attack), which has an RMS of 0.05550. The script erroneously reported this burst window as the closure window in Table 4.

DISC-07.title: Temporal Alignment Discrepancy Across Audio Processing Stages
DISC-07.reported_issue: Older generator clips were described inconsistently as starting at t=0 vs starting at sample 3952.5 (247 ms), and padding differed between centered (older) and right-padded (V4).
DISC-07.root_cause: Traced across all 5 processing stages: (1) In raw generated files, speech starts at t=0 (sample 5, 0.31 ms) for older generator. (2) In normalization, audio_normalizer.py applied center-padding (`pad_left = (16000 - len) // 2` ~ 3950 samples), placing active speech at 247 ms in `audio_16k_1s`. (3) In V4 onset generation, build_onset_aware_data.py padded on the right only (`pad_left = 0`), keeping speech left-aligned at sample 0 (burst at sample 400 = 25 ms). (4) Model loads 16,000 samples directly with zero truncation/padding. (5) Feature extractor computes STFT frames where older speech spans frames 25-75 and V4 spans frames 2-55.

DISC-08.title: SILENCE Centering Truncation Fallback in Diagnostic Transform
DISC-08.reported_issue: In run_alignment_diagnostic.py (Condition A2-B2), the centering logic used `act = np.where(np.abs(a) >= 0.005)[0]` with fallback `last_idx = act[-1] if len(act) > 0 else 8000`. For 25/50 SILENCE clips with peak < 0.005, this truncated the clip to 8,001 samples and zero-padded 3,999 on left and 4,000 on right, omitting 7,999 samples (49.99%) of native ambient noise. For the remaining 25 clips with occasional noise spikes, it truncated trailing samples after the last spike. This violated alignment-only sample preservation.
DISC-08.root_cause: A 1.0s SILENCE clip is an ambient room noise and dither bed spanning 16,000 samples. It lacks an acoustic onset or speech release. Applying an onset detection heuristic (>= 0.005) to ambient noise causes arbitrary truncation. When no defensible onset exists, genuinely alignment-only processing requires preserving the full 16,000-sample ambient recording unshifted.
DISC-08.resolution: Condition A2-B2-V2 implemented in run_alignment_diagnostic_v2.py preserves all 16,000 samples of all 50 SILENCE clips unshifted (0 samples omitted, max abs diff = 0.0, whole-file SHA-256 matches 50/50). All 4 frozen models maintain 0.0% false alarms on SILENCE. Fixed-window ambient noise spectral ratio is 100% invariant.
